definitions.gloss: bitter smile; wry smile; a smile expressing discomfort or awkwardness
definitions.explanation: a smile that conveys a sense of discomfort, embarrassment, irony, or resignation rather than genuine happiness

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{苦笑|にがわら}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{浮|う}かべた→浮かべる：13314_ukaberu⟧。
⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{思|おも}い{出|だ}して→思い出す：01258_omoidasu⟧{苦笑|にがわら}い⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I gave a wry smile remembering my failure.

examples.japanese: ⟦からかわれて→からかう：07353_karakau⟧、{苦笑|にがわら}い⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧しかなかった。
examples.english: I was teased and could only smile bitterly.

notes:
FORMS:
⟦{苦|にが}い→苦い：01201_nigai⟧ (bitter) + ⟦{笑|わら}い→笑い：02641_warai⟧ (smile/laugh) → bitter smile
{苦笑|にがわら}い⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to smile bitterly)
{苦笑|にがわら}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{浮|う}かべる→浮かべる：13314_ukaberu⟧ (to show a bitter smile)

WHEN USED:
- When faced with an awkward situation
- When reminded of past mistakes
- When receiving unwanted but well-meaning advice
- When something is ironically true

TYPES OF SMILES IN JAPANESE:
- ⟦{微笑|ほほえ}み→微笑む：02416_hohoemu⟧ (gentle smile)
- ⟦{愛想笑|あいそうわら}い→愛想笑い：08358_aisouwarai⟧ (polite/forced smile)
- ⟦{作|つく}り{笑|わら}い→作り笑い：08473_tsukuriwarai⟧ (fake smile)
- ⟦{照|て}れ{笑|わら}い→照れ笑い：08460_terewarai⟧ (embarrassed smile)
- ⟦{薄笑|うすわら}い→薄笑い：08455_usuwarai⟧ (smirk)
- ⟦{高笑|たかわら}い→高笑い：08456_takawarai⟧ (loud laugh)

ALTERNATE READING:
⟦{苦笑|くしょう}→苦笑：08688_kushou⟧ is also valid but less common in everyday speech.
